claims.text: Every morning at 06:30 Asia/Jerusalem, culture-rules searches the web for the operator's chosen sections, has Qwen summarise what it found, and delivers one dated newspaper by email (from a culture.dev sender) and as an EPUB queued for the operator's Xteink reader

honesty_conditions.text: A behavioural test drives the whole workflow on fakes (Brave, cortex, Resend, xteink) from a 06:30 Asia/Jerusalem slot to one sent email and one queued item

claims.instruction: Build in this order: actors and action kinds, builtins, the bundle, then the editor; the behavioural test drives the whole workflow on fakes

claims.text: Search goes directly to Brave Search (a 'search' app actor, grant:BRAVE_API_KEY); webglass may become a second backend later (operator, #53)

Summaries are written by Qwen on cortex through a new llm.complete action that calls the Qwen server's OpenAI-compatible endpoint directly: no checkout, no tools; it shares the qwen-spark2 pool, so it waits behind a running PR fix (operator, #53)

Email is sent through Resend with grant:RESEND_API_KEY; the sender domain is chosen from culture.dev or jetson-ai-lab.org (both verified, same key; a drop-down in the editor), default sender no-reply@culture.dev (operator, #53)

The EPUB goes to the xteink library API over the LAN or tailnet with a dedicated xtk_ key the operator mints (create-key newspaper) and stores in grant, and is queued for the operator's device; ebooks-cli takes this over later (operator, #53)
Sections live in one variable, newspaper_sections, holding a JSON string that a builtin parses and validates at the start of each run; a bad value fails the run with a clear error (operator, #53)
A day missed because no node ran at 06:30 is skipped, not caught up (operator, #53)
The newspaper is sent at 06:30 Asia/Jerusalem; its date is that local date (operator, #53)

An 'email' app surface and an email.send action: the actor's connection holds the Resend key reference, the sender domain (one of culture.dev, jetson-ai-lab.org), the sender local part (default no-reply) and a recipient allowlist checked before any secret is read; the action takes to, subject, html and/or text and optional attachments, forwards the engine's idempotency key as Resend's Idempotency-Key, and returns the message id

honesty_conditions.text: A recipient outside the actor's allowlist is refused before the Resend key is read, and the refusal names no secret
A retried send with the same engine idempotency key does not send a second email (Resend Idempotency-Key)

scope_entries.finding: APP_SURFACES is a hard-coded tuple (github, jira, discord) at app_actor.py:36, mirrored in app-config.ts:12; the per-surface connection is unvalidated and the editor's ConnectionField has no enum type, so email/search need new surfaces and the sender domain needs a new drop-down (DiscordTarget in ActionPicker.tsx is the nearest precedent)

the Jira port checks its allowlist before resolving any grant: reference, resolves secrets only at call time, and returns no secret in outputs; assert_refs_only (secrets.py:235) refuses secret literals on save. The email and search ports follow this pattern

http.call can't do it: the secret header value is the whole secret (no 'Bearer ' templating), there is no sender or recipient policy, no attachments or multipart, no parsed results, and the engine's idempotency key isn't forwarded, so dedicated kinds are justified

the non-localhost endpoint check applies to JSON leaves under url/host/endpoint/base_url keys; .py constants (apps/github.py:56) pass, so provider URLs stay in Python and live hosts in actor config, never in committed JSON
cron with an IANA tz is native and fires once per slot mesh-wide, but the event carries only the UTC slot (no local date), and there is no backfill (schedule.py:40-47)
every bridge step requires repo, head_branch and a hex head_sha (agent.py:726-735), and the bridge exposes tools, so a summary step can't use it; hence a direct OpenAI-compatible call
variables hold only a scalar or a flat list of scalars (~42-70), so sections are one JSON string parsed by a builtin
for_each runs a body per item, sequentially, with a required max_iterations and list outputs per port; it fits one search and one summary per section
a pool's cap is the smallest max_concurrency of its enabled actors; an llm actor in qwen-spark2 waits behind a running fix (up to 3900 s), which an early-morning send accepts

POST /api/library takes multipart (file, title, author, kind) with Bearer xtk_, stores EPUB as-is up to 50 MiB and dedupes by sha256; POST /api/devices/{id}/queue takes {item_id}; any xtk_ key is a full operator, so the key is dedicated and revocable
renders EPUB 2 and 3 with an embedded-style toggle and JPG/PNG images; a newspaper should be plain semantic XHTML, one chapter per section
only a scaffold, no ingest API yet, so xteink is the target for now
bundles are actors/, workflows/, rules/ plus seeded variables, imported in that order; trusted digests gate only github.push and review, so the newspaper workflow needs none
